profiles.name: CRANK
profiles.tagline: TEE BOX CHAOS, PUTTER WITH A HEART
profiles.profile: CRANK is basically a rolling argument between the driver and the short game. The driver keeps stabbing him in the ribs, but he’s good enough around the greens to keep the whole thing from exploding, which is why the file keeps showing real contention even when the tee game is actively setting furniture on fire. The recent window has a pretty clear identity: if he can survive the opening act, he’ll hang around and scrap. The bad news is that the opening act is usually loud, crooked, and barely legal.

profiles.name: MattF
profiles.tagline: FAIRWAY POLICE, PUTTING CAUSE OF DEATH UNKNOWN
profiles.profile: MattF is one of those dudes who makes the rest of the card look stupid because the ball just keeps ending up in the right zip code. The driver isn’t screaming for attention, but the total package keeps cashing because he piles up elite-looking tee-to-green work and then sprinkles in just enough putting to avoid turning good golf into tragic golf. There’s some volatility in the scoring punch, but the core identity is simple: hit it in the play area, hit a lot of greens, and let the rest of the field argue with water hazards and their own pride.

profiles.name: Dan94
profiles.profile: Dan94 is the kind of player who can make a course look solvable and then remind you golf is still a dumb game. When the irons are hot, he’s got enough tee speed and approach juice to turn fields inside out, and the scoring ceiling is obvious; the problem is that the same swing shows up wearing two different hats. Some weeks it’s a demolition job, other weeks the bogeys wander in like they own the place. The profile is still clearly elite, but it’s got a little chaos goblin in it.

profiles.name: KeithK75
profiles.tagline: APPROACH GOBLIN WITH A DRIVER PROBLEM
profiles.profile: KeithK75 keeps living in the space between “serious contender” and “why is this harder than it should be?” The irons are the headline: he finds greens, finds looks, and makes enough noise on the scoring side that the rest of the field usually has to play catch-up. But the profile is not clean; there are rounds where the big sticks go sideways and the putter has to keep the whole thing from leaking out through the floorboards. Still, the repeatable shape is nasty enough that you can see why the card keeps circling him near the top instead of letting him drift off into the golf swamp.

profiles.name: BigTime
profiles.profile: BigTime has the body language of a guy trying to hit winners and the scorecard of somebody getting mugged by the greens. The raw power is there, but the window keeps saying the scoring damage usually starts once the ball is parked and the wedges and putter have to actually pay rent. There are enough stretches of competent ball-striking to keep hope alive, but the short-game and putting numbers are doing most of the sabotage. This one is less “mystery slump” and more “the ball-striking keeps opening the door, then the rest of the game kicks the wall in.”

profiles.name: HamSammich
profiles.tagline: SHORT-GAME PANIC IN A BIG SHIRT
profiles.profile: HamSammich is the classic case of a guy who can tease you with one part of the bag and then absolutely torch the rest of it. There are enough good shots in the profile to prove he isn’t hopeless, but the recurring theme is self-inflicted damage: too many doubles, too many extra swings, too much scrambling for oxygen after the hole is already on fire. The putter will occasionally show up and keep things from turning into a total disaster movie, but this file mostly reads like a long-running argument between talent and cleanup duty.
